title: Stashling Item, contract v1
description: One record shape that holds a 3D model, a used-goods listing, a saved link and a video without becoming the union of four schemas. Zones decide who may write what: identity (core), facets (connector, read by every plugin), ext (connector, opaque to core), user (the human, open map), raw (lossless). See docs/ITEM-CONTRACT.md.

id.description: `${source}:${sourceId}` — global, stable, greppable, and namespaced so one store can hold every domain at once without source ids colliding.

sourceId.description: The source's own stable id. Dedup key. NEVER a title.

kind.description: Open vocabulary: video | model | listing | link | …

canonicalUrl.description: Identity: what this is. Tracking params stripped, AMP unwrapped, per-host keep-rules applied. Cross-source dedup key.

byline.description: name and url are OPTIONAL by measurement, not by oversight: on a real 582-row YouTube page 3 rows have no channel name and 19 have a link-less byline anchor. Those are auto-generated bylines, not deleted items.

derived.description: true when computed from the source id rather than scraped. Many sources lazy-load thumbnails, so the URL is not in the DOM at all.

lists.description: Membership is a SCRAPED FACT, not user data: likes | downloads | watch-later | collection:{id}. Merges as a set union across scrapes.

order.description: The source's own sequence, per list. Real information a 'sort by' menu should offer.

tags.description: From the source. User tags live in `user`.

metrics.description: Flat string→finite-number map, and the ONLY thing generic faceting, sorting and gauge plugins read. This is what makes 'print time ≤ 4h' and 'under 30 minutes' the same code path. An absent metric is OMITTED, never stored as 0 — absent and zero must stay distinguishable.

firstSeenAt.description: Takes the EARLIER value on merge.

lastSeenAt.description: Takes the LATER value on merge.

liveness.description: What the SOURCE says about the item. Orthogonal to membership.

evidence.description: WHY: the redirect target, the marker text, the placeholder title. Deleted listings frequently return HTTP 200 with a redirect rather than a 404, so a status-code-only probe reports every deleted item as alive.

retryAfter.description: A terminal state must be re-armable. Re-sighting an item re-arms it.

membership.description: Whether the item is still in YOUR collection. An item can legitimately be liveness:live AND membership:unlisted — still on the site, no longer on your watchlist. Collapsing these two axes loses the difference between 'the platform deleted it' and 'I removed it'.

ext.description: Connector-owned. Core NEVER inspects it. The escape hatch that stops the shared schema from growing: print profiles, price history, word counts, channel ids all live here.

user.description: Human-owned, OPEN MAP, additionalProperties:true BY DESIGN. A connector never writes here. Any writer merges onto what exists and must preserve keys it does not understand — rebuilding this object from a known-key whitelist silently deletes the user's work on round-trip, which is a bug that has bitten this corpus for real.

raw.description: Lossless. Never reconstruct a record from parsed columns. connectorVersion travels with the blob so an older raw can be re-shredded by a newer parser; hash lets a re-import skip unchanged items.
